title: Born in Philadelphia in 1895; father the Biddles' butler
summary: Wooding gives his birth date and Rodman Street home and describes his father's work as butler and steward for the Biddle family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay, this is Chris Albertson interviewing Sam Wooding, April 22, 1975
I think we should start with, Sam, where you were born and when you were born.

Well, Chris, I was born in Philadelphia. June 17, 1895. Well, at that time, most of the black people lived in South Philadelphia, so where we have -- my father was lucky enough to have his own home, it was rather small. But all three of, our four children, were born at 1119 Rodman St., where we grew up until the place had become in such a condition that we couldn't live there because my mother had -- and father had a daughter, and the place had been going rather bad. So he decided to move to another place.
What sort of business was he in?

Well, my father was what we called in those days, a butler. He worked for a very fine family, in fact one of the first families of Philadelphia, the Biddles. He worked at a place on 1420 Walnut St., and there he had to do most all -- he was the butler and the steward and everything else, because he had to do all the buying, he had to wait the tables, and he did all, in fact he was the handyman in the family.
